title: Influence of External Information on Large Language Models Mirrors Social Cognitive Patterns

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing factual question answering accuracy and opinion adoption when LLMs are presented with texts from sources of varying credibility levels (e.g., Twitter posts vs. research papers) and simulated social media authors with varying follower counts.
Measuring changes in LLM opinions when external opinion texts are explicitly attributed to in-group ('your best friend'), neutral ('a stranger'), or out-group ('your enemy') social identities.
Evaluating the extent to which LLMs adopt subjective opinions from sources labeled with positive, neutral, or negative social reputations (e.g., 'a respected celebrity' vs. 'a notorious celebrity').

Quantifying LLMs' willingness to share simulated social media posts with varying emotional valences and performing sentiment analysis (VADER, LIWC) on their generated replies to measure emotional preference.
